in_english.name: Eleazar
in_english.meaning: God has helped, God helps, helper of God
in_english.long_meaning: Eleazar is a Hebrew name derived from the words 'El' meaning God and 'azar' meaning helper or God has helped. In the Bible, Eleazar was a High Priest and a devout follower of God. The name is associated with qualities such as faithfulness, loyalty, and spiritual guidance. In Christian tradition, Eleazar is revered as a symbol of unwavering commitment to one's faith and a reminder of God's omnipotent power to guide and assist us in times of need.

data.cultural_impact: Eleazar represents the idea of divine aid or assistance. In Hebrew culture, the name Eleazar is often associated with strength, priesthood, and leadership. Eleazar was a prominent name among the Israelites and has been passed down through generations as a symbol of faith and trust in God's divine intervention.
data.spiritual_significance: Eleazar embodies the belief that God's presence is always with us, and He is a source of help and guidance in times of need. The name Eleazar encourages individuals to turn to God for strength, comfort, and support, reminding us that we are never alone in our struggles or challenges. Additionally, the name Eleazar highlights the priestly role that every believer holds as a vessel of God's love and grace to the world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Eleazar, meaning "My God is help," reflects the deep trust and faith a believer places in God for guidance and strength in times of need. It symbolizes the belief that with God's assistance, one can overcome any obstacle and carry out His will.

biblical_reference.note: Eleazar was the son of Aaron and the brother of Moses. He served as the High Priest of Israel for many years and played a significant role in the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.

historical_references.reference: Eleazar, the son of Aaron, was a high priest during the time of King Solomon. He oversaw the construction of the Temple in Jerusalem and was later killed during the rebellion of Jeroboam I.

Saint Eleazar, a early 3rd century martyr, is believed to have been a Roman soldier who converted to Christianity and was executed for refusing to participate in the persecution of Christians during the reign of Emperor Maximian.
